internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across nearly every occurrence, God (or, at the mundane level, a human, or even a soul over its own deeds) puts someone or something through an imposed, decisive experience whose function is to bring a latent quality to light. The instrument is polarity-neutral: it can be hardship (fear, hunger, loss, restriction) OR good (honor, provision, a 'good balaa''), so the root does not mean 'afflict' or 'punish'. The purpose is repeatedly spelled out as discrimination or disclosure — 'which of you is best in deed', 'grateful or ungrateful', 'that God may know who fears Him', 'until We know the strivers', laying bare what is in the breasts and the secrets. A single occurrence (20:120, 'a dominion that does not yablaa') stands apart: it is intransitive, has an inanimate subject, and means 'wear out / decay', with no probative content and no Quran-internal bridge to the trial sense.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: blw does NOT entail hardship or suffering (good, honor, provision serve as instruments: 7:168:10:2 bi-l-hasanaat wa-s-sayyi'aat, 21:35:5:2 bi-sh-sharri wa-l-khayr, 89:15:5:1 test by honoring, 8:17:16:1 balaa' hasan). It does NOT entail punishment (even where linked to transgression, 7:163:24:1, the trial is not framed as the penalty). It is NOT the act of knowing — knowing/clarifying is the stated downstream END (5:94:4:2 li-ya'lama, 47:31:1:3 hattaa na'lama, 16:92:22:1 balw THEN bayyana). It does NOT require a divine agent (4:6:1:2 humans assay orphans; 10:30:2:1 a soul assays its own deeds). It does NOT by itself mean 'decay' — that sense is confined to the single intransitive yablaa (20:120:13:1) and is absent from every transitive/derived instance.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 20:120:13:1 (wa-mulkin laa yablaa) is intransitive with an inanimate subject (mulk, dominion), carries no agent, no bi-instrument, and no revealing purpose clause; it means 'wear out / decay / perish' (paired with shajarati l-khuld, the tree of eternity) and its stem-vowel form (yablaa, alif-maqsura, reflecting بلي) differs from the transitive test-verb (yabluu). No Quranic occurrence links this decay sense to the trial sense by shared instrument, subject-type, syntax, or gloss; the lexicographers' 'testing = wearing a thing out' bridge is an external etymological claim and is disallowed under the Quran-internal source policy. It therefore resists unification as a distinct, unbridged intransitive sub-class.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A deeper substrate reading: blw = 'to cause someone/something to undergo a condition/experience, adverse or favorable', with 'test/prove' as its dominant specialization. This is arguably even narrower and handles the good/bad instrument symmetry, the balaa' trial-favor bivalence (8:17:16:1), and the reflexive self-assay of 10:30:2:1 more smoothly. It is not adopted as primary because it under-weights the pervasive discriminative purpose-clause syntax (ayyukum ahsanu 'amalaa; a'ashkuru am akfuru; li-ya'lama; maa fii s-suduur) that is the root's most distinctive Quran-internal feature, and it still fails to cover the intransitive decay at 20:120:13:1. The two accounts sit at an intersection; the honest primary is the manifestation-weighted probative nucleus.

hard_cases.reason: Intransitive 'decay/wear-out' with inanimate subject and no probative content; the only occurrence that prevents a single demonstrated nucleus over all 38.

evidence_basis.statement: 20:120:13:1 (wa-mulkin laa yablaa) is intransitive with an inanimate subject (mulk, dominion), carries no agent, no bi-instrument, and no revealing purpose clause; it means 'wear out / decay / perish' (paired with shajarati l-khuld, the tree of eternity) and its stem-vowel form (yablaa, alif-maqsura, reflecting بلي) differs from the transitive test-verb (yabluu). No Quranic occurrence links this decay sense to the trial sense by shared instrument, subject-type, syntax, or gloss; the lexicographers' 'testing = wearing a thing out' bridge is an external etymological claim and is disallowed under the Quran-internal source policy. It therefore resists unification as a distinct, unbridged intransitive sub-class.

evidence_basis.statement: 10:30:2:1 (tabluu kullu nafsin maa aslafat) inverts the frame: the soul is subject and its own forwarded deeds the object; the probative nucleus ('true state brought to the proof') survives but the God-tests-you agent frame does not.

hard_case_representation.rationale: One genuinely resistant seam (20:120:13:1, intransitive decay, unbridged) plus two bridged boundary/atypicality cases (10:30:2:1 reflexive inversion; 8:17:13:3 good-pole benefaction) are each grounded in cited packet morphology, syntax, and distribution rather than in a prior gloss. rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal demonstration that the intransitive decay sense (20:120:13:1, laa yablaa) and the probative trial sense share one nucleus — e.g. a passage using a transitive blw form to mean 'wear out' or an intransitive yablaa form in a probative context — OR, conversely, evidence that the transitive occurrences split into two or more unbridged trial-senses.
rejection_condition.search_location: The intransitive/derived boundary: 20:120:13:1 against all Form I transitive tokens (e.g. 68:17:2:1 balawnaahum, 7:163:24:1 nabluuhum) and the passive assay tokens (86:9:2:1 tublaa, 3:186:1:2 tublawunna); plus the good-pole tokens 8:17:13:3 / 8:17:16:1 against the affliction tokens 2:155:1:3 / 33:11:2:1.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Compare qac_surface_form_buckwalter stem vowels (yabluu/tublaa transitive vs. yablaa intransitive), argument structure (agent + bi-instrument + purpose clause vs. bare stative predicate), and subject animacy across the cited word_refs; require an actual shared collocation, not an etymological inference.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Exclude external lexica, tafsir, and etymological 'test=wear' bridges (source policy); do not let QAC's homographic collapse of بلو/بلي into one root_id be treated as semantic identity; hold the passive assay uses (86:9, 47:31:7:2) inside the trial nucleus, not as a third sense, since they retain disclosure telos.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If the decay/trial bridge is internally demonstrated, upgrade toward UNIVERSAL/ROOT_GENERALIZATION and possibly STRONG; if the transitive class itself splits, downgrade to UNRESOLVED/multi-class and drop the single-nucleus claim.

reopen_conditions: If a Quranic occurrence is found in which a transitive/derived blw form means 'wear out/decay' or an intransitive yablaa form carries probative content, re-examine whether 20:120:13:1 can be folded into the trial nucleus (upgrade toward UNIVERSAL).

If the passive assay uses (86:9:2:1 tublaa s-saraa'ir, 47:31:7:2 nabluwa akhbaarakum) or the reflexive 10:30:2:1 are shown to form a distinct disclosure-only sense not reducible to the trial nucleus, re-open as a possible multi-class partition.

If the good-pole benefaction reading of 8:17:13:3 / 8:17:16:1 (balaa' hasan) is shown to be a lexicalized 'bestow favor' sense unbridged to the trial verbs, re-open the noun cluster's CONSISTENT disposition.
